content: The carboxypeptidase N catalytic chain is an enzyme encoded by the CPN1 gene in humans. This enzyme is a plasma metalloprotease that specifically removes basic amino acids from the C-terminal end of peptides and proteins. It plays a critical role in regulating bioactive peptides, such as kinins and anaphylatoxins, and is also referred to as kininase-1 or anaphylatoxin inactivator due to its functional properties. Structurally, the enzyme exists as a tetramer, consisting of two identical regulatory subunits and two identical catalytic subunits, with the CPN1 gene encoding the catalytic subunit. Mutations in the CPN1 gene can lead to conditions such as angioedema or chronic urticaria, which are associated with carboxypeptidase N deficiency. Additionally, in melanocytic cells, the expression of the CPN1 gene may be regulated by the microphthalmia-associated transcription factor (MITF).
